name: Section Library
summary: Shopify app that adds 200+ ready-made theme sections plus AI-generated custom ones (Gemini 3.1 Pro), all inside the native theme editor so layouts change without a developer. Live since October 2023 with a single App Store review.
best_for: Shopify merchants who want ready-made theme sections and the occasional AI-generated layout inside the native theme editor, and who can live with an app that has almost no public track record
skip_if: you are rebuilding a store you cannot afford to break and want a page builder with thousands of merchants behind it, or you need your monthly cost known in advance: the credit unit is never defined
honest_knock:
Almost three years on the App Store and one review. The app launched 10 October 2023 and, as of 5 October 2026, exactly one merchant has written about it: a five-star note from October 2023 by someone who had it installed for four minutes. That is not evidence of quality and not evidence of trouble: it is an absence of evidence, and on an app that writes sections into your live theme, that absence is the main thing to weigh. On the same listing page Shopify shows Section Store with 2,967 reviews (read 5 October 2026), also free to install, which is what a track record looks like in this category. The old site, sectionlibrary.com, still answers with Shopify’s “Store unavailable” page (17 September, 5 October and 12 November 2026); the product now lives at optifyapps.com/mason under its new name, Mason.

Second, the credit is undefined. Every plan is priced in credits and nothing on the listing says what one buys, so you cannot price your own usage before you commit.

Third, the AI half of the product is Google's. The October listing named Gemini 3.1 Pro, and the Mason privacy policy (effective 24 October 2026) says prompts, the detected brand kit and the relevant theme content go to third-party AI model providers such as Google's Gemini models, so output quality and consistency shift when Google ships a new model, which is outside the vendor's hands as much as yours. The library half, the 200+ pre-built sections, is the part that depends on nobody else, and it is the part worth judging the app on.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · per month for 25 credits and access to the full section library, billed every 30 days in USD
pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-09-17, 2026-10-05 and 2026-11-12 on apps.shopify.com/section-library; listed in October as “Section Library: AI Sections” and on 12 November 2026 as “Mason: AI Page Builder”; every amount is unchanged since 19 August 2026) Free plan: 8 credits a month, access to the free sections only, basic AI generation. Starter $9 a month: 25 credits, all sections accessible, AI section generation, email support. Pro $19 a month: 55 credits, all sections, priority support. Business $29 a month: 90 credits, all sections, priority support. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and the listing shows no free trial on the paid tiers — the free plan is the trial. One thing the pricing table still never states is what a credit actually buys. Whether one credit is one AI generation, one section added to a theme, or something else is defined nowhere on the listing — and the credit count is the only thing separating the four plans. The old site, sectionlibrary.com, answered HTTP 402 with Shopify’s “Store unavailable” page on 17 September, 5 October and 12 November 2026. The product now has a page at optifyapps.com/mason (read 12 November 2026), which says Section Library is now Mason: the same app from the same team, repositioned as an AI page builder that generates full pages and custom sections from a prompt on top of the section library. That page repeats the free plan (8 AI credits a month) and paid plans from $9, and it does not define a credit either. Developer Optify, 16 Rue Cuvier, Lyon, France; the app launched 10 October 2023. It still carries a 5.0 rating from exactly one App Store review, left in October 2023 by a merchant who had the app installed for four minutes; still the only review on 12 November 2026.
